## Summary

Haloform oxidation of 4-acetylbiphenyl gives biphenyl-4-carboxylic acid. This is sample data; the quantities are not experimentally verified.

## Reagents

| Reagent | CAS | MW (g/mol) | Amount | mmol | Equiv |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4-Acetylbiphenyl | 92-91-1 | 196.25 | 1.962 g | 10 | 1.0 |
| Sodium hypochlorite | 7681-52-9 | 74.44 | 1 M aqueous solution, 50 mL | 50 | 5.0 |
| Sodium hydroxide | 1310-73-2 | 40.00 | 0.800 g | 20.0 | 2.0 |
| Sodium hydrogen sulfite | 7631-90-5 | 104.06 | aqueous solution, as needed | – | – |
| Hydrogen chloride | 7647-01-0 | 36.46 | 2 M, as needed | – | – |
| Ethyl acetate | 141-78-6 | 88.11 | for washing the alkaline solution, as needed | – | – |
| Heptane | 142-82-5 | 100.21 | a little for TLC | – | – |

## Procedure

1. Dissolve sodium hydroxide in the aqueous sodium hypochlorite solution; place the strongly alkaline solution and 4-acetylbiphenyl in a flask.
2. Stir vigorously and warm to about 70 °C in a fume hood.
3. Maintain the temperature and monitor conversion by TLC (heptane–ethyl acetate 2:1).
4. Cool the mixture and add aqueous sodium hydrogen sulfite until residual oxidant is destroyed.
5. Wash the alkaline mixture with ethyl acetate and separate the aqueous layer.
6. Slowly acidify the aqueous layer with 2 M hydrochloric acid, then cool in ice.

## Workup and Purification

Collect the precipitated acid by suction filtration, wash with cold water and dry. Collect the organic wash as halogenated waste because it contains chloroform. Expected yield: 1.39 g (7.00 mmol, 70 %).

## Characterization

White solid; expected IR bands near 1700 cm⁻¹ (C=O) and a broad carboxylic acid O–H band.

## Notes

1. Stir vigorously to improve contact between phases.
2. Destroy residual hypochlorite before acidification to avoid chlorine release.
3. The haloform reaction produces chloroform; work in a hood.

## Hazards and Waste Disposal

Sodium hydroxide causes severe burns and eye damage. Chloroform is formed during the reaction; it is harmful and suspected of causing cancer. Heptane is highly flammable and hazardous to the environment. 4-Acetylbiphenyl: may irritate skin and eyes; Sodium hypochlorite: corrosive oxidant; releases chlorine with acid; Sodium hydrogen sulfite: harmful if swallowed; releases sulfur dioxide with acid; Hydrogen chloride: acidic solution irritates or burns skin and eyes; Ethyl acetate: highly flammable; eye irritant; Biphenyl-4-carboxylic acid: may irritate skin and eyes. Work in a fume hood; wear gloves and eye protection. Collect chloroform-containing organic washings as halogenated waste and aqueous filtrates separately.
